claim.why_it_matters: In the PDF the 1./2. locale cases are indented under each of b), c) and d) (8.8.4.1.3.3 GR2); the markdown places them at the same indentation as b), c), d), detaching them from their parent items.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 133 (PDF p155) indents items 1./2. one level deeper than b), c) and d). The markdown puts them at the same 3-space indent, but nothing is missing or misplaced. Every 1./2. pair follows its own parent item in the same order as the PDF, and the wording matches word for word. The numbering styles also differ (letters for the items, digits for the sub-items), so the hierarchy is still unambiguous: each 1./2. pair can only belong to the lettered item just before it. This is an indentation-only formatting difference that does not change meaning, so it is not a content discrepancy.
